newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana president leaves for medical checks in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Guyana president leaves for medical checks in U.S..

text.p: Guyana's President Cheddi Jagan left for the United States on Saturday for medical tests after being taken to hospital suffering from heart problems, government officials said.

Jagan, 78, left the Timehri airport aboard a U.S. military aircraft which was due to take him to Panama and thence to Washington for tests at the Walter Reed hospital in Maryland, Health Minister Gail Teixiera said.
His doctor, Hughley Hanoman said the tests would determine whether the president required surgery.
Jagan was rushed to the the state-run Georgetown hospital on Friday night after complaining of "feeling unwell and chest pains," Teixiera told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
Reporters said Jagan smiled and waved as he left hospital on a stretcher before being taken to the airport. Hanoman said the president had no history of heart problems.

Jagan led his People's Progressive Party (PPP) to victory at the polls in October 1992 -- Guyana's first democratic elections for 28 years. He was previously premier of British Guiana from 1961 to 1964 before Guyana gained independence in 1966.
